issues: The notes say 'Registration year = the January in which brokers registered'. That is imprecise. The yearly files include late registrations made during the rest of the year. In registry2024.csv, 409 of the 543 rows have a 'Completion time' in January 2024. The other 134 were completed from February to December 2024, and one on 18 January 2025. The year label is the annual registry year, not the month of registration.
The 2026 registry is a live file. The page reads 'Last Updated: 7/29/2026', so the 603 count applies to that version and may change.

Checked and correct: I downloaded all four CSVs linked from the registry page and recounted them. registry.csv (the 2026 registry, download name 'California Data Broker Registry 2026.csv') has 603 data rows with 603 distinct names. registry2024.csv has 543 rows (542 distinct names; 'BoardEx, LLC' appears twice). registry2025.csv has 543 rows after a note row and a header row (540 distinct names). complete-reg-data-brokers.csv (the 2020-2023 DOJ file) has 549 rows. All four quotes were re-fetched and FOUND. The DROP dates (1 January 2026 for consumers, 1 August 2026 for broker processing) match the page.

fieldFixes.notes: Year = the annual registry the broker appears in. Registration is due 1-31 January and covers the previous calendar year, but late registrations are added through the year: in the 2024 file, 409 of 543 rows were completed in January 2024 and 134 later. 2020-2023 registrations were run by the California Department of Justice and are published as one combined file (549 rows), so they are not split by year here. Since 1 January 2026 Californians can send one deletion request to every registered broker through the DROP platform (the Delete Act), and brokers must process requests from 1 August 2026. Counts are rows in CalPrivacy's own CSV downloads, computed by this study; the 2026 file is the version on the registry page marked 'Last Updated: 7/29/2026'.

issues: The notes list the wrong annual totals. They say the 2022-2024 estimates come from 'nearly EUR 1.1bn, EUR 1.64bn, EUR 1.78bn'. The back-calculation from the January 2025 cumulative figure (EUR 5.88bn) actually subtracts EUR 1.2bn (year from 28 Jan 2024), EUR 1.78bn (from 28 Jan 2023) and EUR 1.64bn (from 28 Jan 2022). That gives 4.68, 2.90 and 1.26, which match the plotted points. The EUR 1.1bn figure is only used in the forward-sum cross-check.

The notes for points 2022-2024 say 'DLA Piper did not state a cumulative figure in this edition'. That is only confirmed for the public web summaries: the 2022, 2023 and 2024 pages state no cumulative total. The full reports sit behind a registration form (inform.dlapiper.com / inform-new.dlapiper.com 'download the report' landing pages), so I could not check whether they state one. The wording should be limited to the public page.
The 2021 point's source title is wrong. The page title is 'DLA Piper GDPR fines and data breach survey: January 2021', not '... survey 2021'.

Checked and correct: all 10 quotes were re-fetched with a fresh cache and FOUND. Page dates match: 20 Jan 2020, 19 Jan 2021, 18 Jan 2022, 25 Jan 2023, 17 Jan 2024, 21 Jan 2025 and 21 Jan 2026. EUR 272.5m is cumulative since 25 May 2018; it agrees with the 2022 page's 'nearly a sevenfold increase on last year's total' (1.1bn / (272.5m - 114m) ≈ 6.9). The arithmetic is right: 5.88-1.2=4.68, -1.78=2.90, -1.64=1.26. The forward sum 0.2725+1.1+1.64+1.78+1.2 = 5.99 is about EUR 0.1bn above 5.88, as the notes say. The 2026 total of EUR 7.1bn runs to 10 January 2026. The CMS figures (2,685 fines, about EUR 6.11bn, cut-off 1 March 2026) were FOUND. The countries surveyed (EU-27 plus UK, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein) are stated on the 2022 and 2023 pages. The EUR 1.2bn Meta fine in 2023 is confirmed on the 2024 page.

fieldFixes.notes: Totals are as at each annual January survey, so '2026' means fines to 10 January 2026. The 2022-2024 points are estimates computed by this study. They subtract DLA Piper's stated annual totals (EUR 1.64bn for the year from 28 January 2022, EUR 1.78bn from 28 January 2023, EUR 1.2bn from 28 January 2024) from its January 2025 cumulative figure (EUR 5.88bn). An independent count, CMS's GDPR Enforcement Tracker (publicly known fines only), gives about EUR 6.11bn across 2,685 fines to 1 March 2026. That is lower than DLA Piper's EUR 7.1bn, a reminder that the totals depend on method.
